overview: This table sets which titles players can show on their player cards and how each title appears.
description: Defines the player-card title choices: each row joins a title row ID to an Item row that gates ownership and to an ItemText key used for the localized display label.

Id.simple: The name that connects a saved player card to this title. A card shows the starting title if it cannot use the saved one.
Id.technical: FName. The save/online customization struct stores it as TitleId, and FGamePlayerCardParameter::InitializeFromSave copies it into FGamePlayerCardParameter::TitleId; the customization constructor defaults it to '10'. Every exported key is a decimal string (10-7030). Validate() replaces an unknown or None ID with '10', and PlayerCard_ResetUnownedIds() uses the owned-title test to do the same. The leaderboard packer converts the ID with FCString::Atoi into uint16 TitleNumber; the unpacker rebuilds it with FString::FromInt and falls back to '10' if no row exists. Lookups scan PlayerCardTitleDataTables and take the first matching row; the player-card and customize widgets use this ID for lookup and selection.

Id_Item.simple: Chooses the item a player must own and unlock before the title appears in customization.
Id_Item.technical: FName. PlayerCard_FindTitleItem resolves it against ItemDataTables by Item row ID; the exported title items carry this ID and have VariableId 'None', unlike emblem/plate item links. The customize tile widget checks the linked item's stock bNew flag and clears it through the resolved Item row. PlayerCard_GetOwnedTitleRows keeps rows with Id_Item == None and removes other rows unless a Title item with that ID has positive stock and GameItem_IsRowUnlocked passes (a negative UserProgressFlag is always unlocked; otherwise the progress word bit must be set). With bSort it stably sorts the surviving rows by that Item row's SortingOrder. The title-text twin fallback searches all title rows for another row with the same non-None Id_Item and a different Id; the supplied export has no such pair.

Id_ItemText.simple: Chooses the words shown for this title. The customization list needs the title in the player's language, and a blank name shows a generic label.
Id_ItemText.technical: FName. GameItem_GetNameTextCore is called with EGameItemType::Title, which does no Title-specific ID rewrite, and HasGameTextContent checks whether the current-language GameText row for that key has non-empty text. All 227 export keys are present and non-empty in each of the 11 ItemTextDataTable language shards. The customize tile filter keeps rows whose key is None or resolves to text and drops only non-None keys with no text; None-key tiles use SYS_CUSTOMIZE_PLAYERCARD_LABEL_0011. PlayerCard_MakeTitleTextRequest checks the plain key first and, only when it has no text while Id_Item is non-None and bUseTwin is true, substitutes the Id_ItemText of the first other row across all title rows with the same Id_Item and a different Id; otherwise it uses this row's key.

notes: The export has one 227-row variant. Every row key and ID is numeric (10-7030); each Id_Item and Id_ItemText is unique and follows ITM_TITLE_<four-digit ID>. All 227 Id_Item values resolve in ItemDataTable to EGameItemType::Title rows with SortingOrder and the same Id_ItemText; their VariableId is 'None'.

Because no two exported title rows share an Id_Item, the title-text twin fallback is inert for the supplied data. The nickname table instead has 2,940 rows over 982 items with up to three text variants per item.

PlayerCard_GetOwnedTitleRows starts from every row in the table array, removes rows with an owned-item check failure except Id_Item == None, and optionally stable-sorts by the linked Item row's SortingOrder (first table hit). No shipped row uses a None Id_Item, so the sort comparator's unguarded Item lookup is not exercised by the export.

The tile list additionally removes rows with a non-None Id_ItemText that has no current-language text, deduplicates by resolved text within each Id_Item, and can show the selected row's Id on a same-item tile when that selected row is not represented in the unique displayed rows.

'10' is the constructor default and the repeated fallback for invalid, unknown, unowned, or unrecoverable leaderboard IDs. The leaderboard field is a uint16; all shipped IDs fit it and are decimal, so the Atoi/FromInt round trip is exact.

Runtime statements are traced in the local reconstruction, whose comments record retail RVAs. No retail Blueprint graphs or editor-only tools were available, so this does not claim exhaustive Blueprint or editor-tool coverage.

usages.detail: After all primary asset loaders complete, Tick resolves the PlayerCardTitleDataTable asset and appends it to PlayerCardTitleDataTables (+0xA90); the loader name is registered at :472.
GetRows enumerates all rows of every loaded table; it backs PlayerCard_GetAllTitleRows, the owned-title list, and the sorted customize list.
Validate() checks TitleId with bCheckNone=true across the title-table array and resets a missing or None row to '10'.
PlayerCard_GetOwnedTitleRows filters all rows by owned/unlocked Title items and optionally stable-sorts by the linked Item SortingOrder.
PlayerCard_IsTitleOwned scans that owned-row list by Id; ResetUnownedIds (:322) and tile selection use it to accept or reset a title.
PlayerCard_FindTitleItem resolves a title row's Id_Item to the Item row used for new-flag state.
PlayerCard_MakeTitleTextRequest builds the localized label request and, under its no-text/non-None-item/bUseTwin conditions, uses another row with the same Id_Item.
Builds title selection tiles from owned rows, filters untranslated non-None keys, deduplicates by text per item, applies the fallback label, new flags, and selected-row substitution.
Resolves the saved TitleId row into a text request for the player card; the widget substitutes '10' for an invalid ID before the call (:111).
Leaderboard unpack converts uint16 TitleNumber to a decimal FName and validates the row, otherwise uses '10'.
Leaderboard pack converts the save card's TitleId with Atoi into the packed uint16 TitleNumber.
TitleId is written as a fixed-width FName in the save at +0xC and read back at :481.
Owned Title items come from StudioItemStocks entries with positive Count whose Item row type is Title; unlock state is tested at :206.
